JACKIE JOHNSON.record: Was the top state prosecutor in Glynn County when Ahmaud Arbery was shot in February 2020. Her office recused within days because Gregory McMichael had worked as an investigator in her office and called her after the shooting; she recommended neighboring Waycross DA George Barnhill take over, and, per TheGrio's summary of the AG investigation, did not disclose that Barnhill had already advised police. Two Glynn County commissioners told the AJC she told police not to arrest the McMichaels; she denied this and blamed police. She lost the November 2020 general election with 47.3% to independent Keith Higgins, a loss she largely blamed on the Arbery controversy. Indicted in September 2021 (after AG Chris Carr ordered an investigation) on a felony count of violating her oath of office and a misdemeanor count of obstructing police. At her February 2025 trial, Senior Judge John R. Turner acquitted her of the obstruction count, saying prosecutors had not shown "one scintilla of evidence" she directed police not to arrest the shooter, and then dismissed the oath-of-office count as fatally flawed by technical errors, ending the case. Earlier in her tenure she drew criticism over the 2011 grand jury review of the police shooting of Caroline Small and oversaw the investigation of former Glynn County police chief John Powell, whose charges the state Supreme Court later invalidated (per The Current). AJC columnist Bill Torpy wrote that she was seeking a fourth term in 2020 and lost 'largely because of her connection to the case of Ahmaud Arbery,' and also cited her 2018 deal releasing Cory Sasser, who later killed his estranged wife and a friend.
